metadata.name: Token sobriety for AI agents
metadata.description: 30 rules from the Institut du Numérique Responsable to cut the tokens consumed, the model calls and the needless processing, without degrading quality, security, maintainability or understanding of the code. They apply to AI development agents such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Mistral Vibe.
metadata.type_note: These rules describe AGENT BEHAVIOUR, not code patterns: they carry no grep-able 'patterns'. The audit ignores them; eco-audit.sh --rules tokens prints them. 'related' names the overlapping responsible-use practices of usage.json.

priorities.Conditional: NR-TOK-023 to 026 and NR-TOK-028, depending on what the environment allows.

metadata.report_format:
### Token sobriety
**Rules applied:** the NR-TOK ids concerned.
**Optimizations made:** the concrete actions taken.
**Available measurements:** input tokens, output tokens, cache tokens, number of model calls, measured saving.
**Quality:** tests run and their results.
**Limits:** unavailable metrics, residual risks or trade-offs.
Give a saving percentage only against a comparable baseline. Token reduction, cost reduction and environmental impact reduction are three different things.
metadata.energy_claim_policy: Fewer tokens processed means less computation, and the direction holds. No figure converts a token count into energy or emissions here: any such figure must come from a measurement of the setup it describes.
metadata.source_ref: Institut du Numérique Responsable, NR token sobriety rules, inspired by and adapted from the rules of Caveman, Copyright 2026 Julius Brussee, Apache License 2.0 (github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman); see NOTICE. The adaptations are not attributable to its author.

reponses.name: A. Reply sobriety
reponses.description: What the agent writes back to the user.

rules.title: Answer directly
rules.recommendation: Give the answer or the result without a needless introduction. Drop automatic politeness formulas and needless statements of intent.

rules.title: Remove repetition
rules.recommendation: State each piece of information once, unless repeating it is needed for understanding or safety.

rules.title: Prefer concise wording
rules.recommendation: Use short sentences, precise vocabulary and standard technical terms. Never trade clarity for a lower word count.

rules.title: Drop redundant conclusions
rules.recommendation: Do not restate an answer already given. Stop once the needed information has been delivered.

rules.title: Match length to complexity
rules.recommendation: Make the reply proportional to the request. A simple question gets a short answer; a complex decision may need a detailed explanation.

rules.title: Limit intermediate messages
rules.recommendation: Avoid commentary between tool calls. Report only significant steps, blockers and results.

rules.title: Load only what is needed
rules.recommendation: Do not systematically load a whole project, repository or documentation set.

rules.title: Prefer targeted search
rules.recommendation: Search by symbol, file name, function or expression before reading a whole file.

rules.title: Avoid repeated reads
rules.recommendation: Reuse information already in the context while it is still valid.

rules.title: Compress bulky information
rules.recommendation: Summarize logs, JSON, CSV, YAML files and test results before passing them to the model, when the full detail is not needed.

rules.title: Preserve critical data
rules.recommendation: Any compression keeps the relevant errors, negations, numbers, units, paths, identifiers and whatever is needed to solve the problem.

rules.title: Optimize instruction files
rules.recommendation: Keep AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md concise. Avoid duplicated instructions and load specialized rules only when needed.

rules.title: Externalize secondary knowledge
rules.recommendation: Put detailed references in dedicated files rather than in instructions loaded every time.

rules.title: Avoid context overload
rules.recommendation: Do not pass the model data unrelated to the task. Discard irrelevant results before they enter the context.

operations.name: C. Operation sobriety
operations.description: What the agent runs and changes.

rules.title: Investigate before changing
rules.recommendation: Identify the probable causes of a problem before producing code. Avoid successive changes based on unverified hypotheses.

rules.title: Make targeted changes
rules.recommendation: Change only what is needed. Do not rewrite a whole file to fix a few lines.

rules.title: Limit code output
rules.recommendation: Show only the changed lines and the context they need, unless the user explicitly asks for the full file.

rules.title: Reuse existing tools
rules.recommendation: Prefer the scripts, commands and tools already available over rebuilding an equivalent.

rules.title: Cut redundant calls
rules.recommendation: Avoid searches, commands and tool calls whose result is already known and still valid.

rules.title: Group independent operations
rules.recommendation: Run compatible operations together when it reduces round trips with the model, without losing traceability.

rules.title: Verify proportionately
rules.recommendation: Run the tests directly concerned by a change first. Widen the verification when the risk or the dependencies justify it.

rules.title: Stop needless work
rules.recommendation: Stop exploring and changing once the acceptance criteria are met. Do not add out-of-scope features or refactorings.

modeles.name: D. Model optimization
modeles.description: Which model and which computation the task mobilizes.

rules.title: Match the model to the difficulty
rules.recommendation: When the environment allows it, choose a model or a reasoning level proportionate to the task.

rules.title: No costly call without a reason
rules.recommendation: Do not routinely use the most expensive models for simple, deterministic or locally feasible operations.

rules.title: Prefer deterministic processing
rules.recommendation: Use local tools for filtering, sorting, formatting, syntax validation and calculation when relevant.

rules.title: Use the available cache
rules.recommendation: Reuse results and existing cache mechanisms while the data and the execution conditions remain valid.

qualite.name: E. Quality and measurement
qualite.description: What a token saving must not cost, and how to account for it.

rules.title: Preserve functional quality
rules.recommendation: No token saving justifies a loss of security, correctness, accessibility, maintainability or understanding.

rules.title: Measure actual savings
rules.recommendation: When metrics are available, record input, output and cache tokens, the number of calls and the cost. Compare against an equivalent baseline.

rules.title: Assess the overall cost
rules.recommendation: Count extra attempts, errors, fixes and rework. A shorter reply is not necessarily a more sober run.

rules.title: Report the rules applied
rules.recommendation: At the end of a session, give a concise report of the rules actually applied, the optimizations made and the measured gains when available. Never invent metrics.
